survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The ICILS 2013 international database is based on a multistage stratified cluster sample of schools, with students and teachers nested within schools. For student-level analyses, analysts are instructed to use the total student weight TOTWGTS (and for school-level analyses TOTWGTC; for teacher-level analyses TOTWGTT). The guide also provides jackknife repeated replication (JRR) variance estimation support via replicate weights and jackknife zone/replicate variables (e.g., SRWGT1–SRWGT75 and JKZONES/JKREPS for students), and recommends using the IEA IDB Analyzer because it automatically applies the correct weights and replication structure. Plausible values for the CIL achievement scale are handled via multiple imputation (five PVs), so any achievement analysis must combine results across PVs while still using the complex-survey weights/replication for correct standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This user guide documents plausible values (five IRT-based imputed CIL scores) and the need to replicate analyses across PVs, but it does not specify a single explicit missing-data imputation/deletion rule for questionnaire item nonresponse in the way required by the extraction schema. Instead, it describes coding conventions for omitted/not-administered/not-reached responses and notes that multiple imputation methods can be an option for missing data issues, without committing to one method for all analyses. Therefore, missing-data handling is treated as not reported at the paper level.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The public-use international database includes only records that satisfy international sampling standards and adjudication. Schools are included if the principal and/or ICT-coordinator responded (school-level participation is independent of student/teacher participation). Students are included if they responded to at least one item of the student test and at least 50% of sampled students in that school participated; students with technical failures preventing completion are excluded. Teachers are included if they responded to the teacher questionnaire and at least 50% of sampled teachers in that school participated; teacher data from schools with <50% teacher participation are excluded. Additional exclusions include records reported as out of scope/not eligible/excluded, and any unreliable or undocumented records; questionnaire items not administered due to rotated test design or technical failures are coded as not administered.

data.outcome_summary: This document is a user guide for the ICILS 2013 international database, not an empirical study estimating effects with machine learning. It describes the ICILS 2013 design: a multistage stratified cluster sample of schools with nested student and teacher samples, and a rotated computer-based assessment where students complete only subsets of test modules. Student achievement in computer and information literacy (CIL) is produced using IRT scaling and multiple imputation via five plausible values (PV1–PV5), requiring analysts to run analyses separately for each PV and combine results using Rubin-style rules. The guide also specifies complex-survey estimation requirements: analysts should use the appropriate total weights (TOTWGTS for students, TOTWGTT for teachers, TOTWGTC for schools) and jackknife repeated replication (JRR) replicate weights/zone variables for correct standard errors. It further documents coding conventions for missingness (omitted vs not administered vs not reached) and cautions against causal language because the design is observational and cross-sectional.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for a technical user guide/data documentation rather than a research article with an empirical ML prediction task. As a result, there are no model training algorithms, no target variables predicted by ML, and no performance metrics/effects to tabulate. The guide focuses on how to correctly analyze ICILS 2013 data (weights, replication, PVs, coding of missingness), so the ML and findings sections are intentionally empty.
